sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Olivet, a commune on the south bank of the Loire next to Orléans, keeps its parking free. The commune's page says it has over 600 spaces, 430 of them in the town centre, and that all parking is free but time-limited, in three zones: red with 20 minutes, blue with 1h30 on a disc, and white with no limit, where abusive parking is sanctioned after seven days [0]. It names 11 town-centre car parks, from Mairie and Marcel Belot to Arcades and Marronniers, without naming an operator [1]. In a magazine of June 2017 the commune said it did not plan new centre car parks but would optimise existing ones with better signage and adjusted bays, and that parking would stay free everywhere; the fine for overstaying a blue or red bay was then 17 euros [3]. Orléans Métropole's own parking page speaks of paid on-street zones, a free 15-minute stay and a 25-euro post-parking charge, but presents these as its offer in Orléans and does not mention Olivet [7]. Its aim is to reduce solo driving in favour of tram, bus and active modes and to encourage long stays in car parks and short stays on the street [7]. The urban mobility plan runs from 2019 to 2028, to be replaced by a first mobility plan in 2028 [8].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development to watch is the centre project Éclosion, about 300 homes and a pedestrian mall between place Louis Sallé and the Poutyl park, with a commune contribution of 18.3 million euros and a café-restaurant due at the end of 2027 or early 2028; the page mentions a landscaped car park among the changes of December 2024 [14]. The slides of the public meeting of 12 December 2024 showed a proposed landscaped car park on rue Paul Genain with 40 blue-zone spaces, forecast to enter service in September or October 2025 at an estimated 500,000 euros excluding VAT, and an amendment to the development concession still had to go to the council. This was a proposal, and we found no source saying whether it opened [13]. On charging, the Métropole's open data list two stations in Olivet, rue de l'Yvette and 238 rue du Général de Gaulle, each with two 22 kW points, in service since 15 July 2021, in a dataset last updated in July 2023 [10]. The Métropole charges 0.50 euro per kWh from 1 January 2024 with a flat fee of 25 euros against long stays, and counts 30 of its charge points across the 22 communes, but the page names no stations [11].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Three park-and-rides serve tram line A in Olivet, Zénith near the Parc des Expositions, Victor Hugo and Les Aulnaies, where a validated Tao ticket gives access and the P+R ticket gives unlimited parking plus a return fare for up to seven people [5]. In the Métropole's open data, Victor Hugo has 141 spaces and Les Aulnaies 244, both with Effia stationnement as manager and live availability, while Zénith, with 190 spaces, is filed under Orléans [4]. In October 2024 the Métropole chose Keolis to run the Tao services for six years from 1 January 2025, and the press release lists park-and-rides in the contract, which the open data's Effia label does not explain [15]. Tram line A is 18 km with 24 stations, running every 5.5 minutes at peak [9]. The only study of centre use is from 2017, by IPROCIA, which found the supply well sized, with saturation peaks on market day, Saturday late morning and school exit times, and every centre car park within five minutes' walk of the shops; it may no longer hold [2]. A 2024 Métropole report charts park-and-ride attendance from 2018 to 2023, but we could not read the figures [6].

Our data cover the two Olivet park-and-rides in the feed, for 17 days since 5 October 2026. Victor Hugo averaged about 29% on weekdays and 17% at weekends, with a peak of 65% on a Thursday afternoon. Les Aulnaies averaged 1% on weekdays and about 0% at weekends and peaked at 7%, so it is almost always empty. Zénith and the free centre car parks are not in our data.
